tina: Observed a nasty onboarding storm with the Python sample-app. When the client pages embeddings it often gets a 401 from auth rotation, triggers immediate retries across ~10 coroutines, and we end up with a huge spike of requests that trips quota. Repro + logs below.

kai: Is this happening only on long-running sessions or during the very first paging run? Any correlation with sts/kms calls?

tina: Happens during first few minutes of a new session (warm start). Repro steps: start sample-app with default py-sdk settings (max_concurrency=10, page_window=12), kick off the onboarding that requests 6 pages concurrently. After ~20s the token returned by our auth proxy rotates (short-lived), some requests see 401, each coroutine triggers a token refresh + immediate retry. Because we don't singleflight refreshes and we return permits immediately on error, the other coroutines grab tokens and flood again. Logs:
```
[2026-03-22T17:12:02Z] request id=aa11 page=1 -> 200
[2026-03-22T17:12:03Z] request id=aa12 page=2 -> 401 auth_expired
[2026-03-22T17:12:03Z] auth: refresh start (caller=aa12)
[2026-03-22T17:12:03Z] request id=aa13 page=3 -> 401 auth_expired
[2026-03-22T17:12:03Z] auth: refresh start (caller=aa13)
[2026-03-22T17:12:03Z] client: retry immediate page=2
[2026-03-22T17:12:03Z] client: retry immediate page=3
[2026-03-22T17:12:03Z] server: quota-check async -> 429 (no Retry-After)
[2026-03-22T17:12:03Z] client: retry immediate page=2
[2026-03-22T17:12:04Z] auth: refresh done (caller=aa12)
[2026-03-22T17:12:04Z] auth: refresh done (caller=aa13)
```
Note: server didn't set Retry-After because quota check runs async; our py-sdk treat lack of header as 0 and retries immediately. Also we run token refresh without a singleflight lock so multiple refreshes occur in parallel which is noisy.

rob: Two related issues then: (1) retry-on-401 semantics + lack of backoff (2) concurrent token refreshes. Both amplify when pagination is concurrent.

ana: small nit: naming <client-token-window> vs <token-pool> is confusing in the sample app README. We should document recommended values for onboarding vs production.

kai: Proposal: immediate fixes in SDK and sample-app: 1) implement a singleflight lock around token refresh so only one coroutine refreshes and others await result 2) interpret missing Retry-After as min_backoff_ms=400 and add jitter +-250ms 3) when a request fails with 401 or 429, don't return window permits immediately; mark them as cooldown for 800ms 4) lower sample-app defaults to max_concurrency=3, page_window=4 for onboarding flow.

tina: I sketched a tiny asyncio-friendly snippet that worked in local smoke tests — it collapsed parallel refreshes into one and smoothed retries. Pseudo:```py
# py-sdk/auth.py
import asyncio, random, time
_refresh_lock = None

async def get_token():
    global _refresh_lock
    if _refresh_lock is None:
        _refresh_lock = asyncio.Lock()
    # fast-path: valid token cached
    if token_cache.valid():
        return token_cache.get()
    # only one refresh runs
    async with _refresh_lock:
        if token_cache.valid():
            return token_cache.get()
        new = await _do_refresh()  # network call
        token_cache.set(new, expires_at=time.time()+new.ttl)
        return new

# backoff helper
def parse_retry_after(header):
    try:
        v = float(header)
        if v >= 1.0:
            return int(v*1000)
    except Exception:
        pass
    # missing or <1s -> default 400ms + jitter
    return 400 + int(random.random()*250)

# when a request fails, put permits into cooldown before reusing
class PermitPool:
    def __init__(self):
        self.available = []
        self.cooldowns = []  # list of (ready_at, permit)

    def return_with_cooldown(self, permit, cooldown_ms=800):
        ready = int(time.time()*1000) + cooldown_ms
        self.cooldowns.append((ready, permit))

    async def refill_loop(self):
        while True:
            now = int(time.time()*1000)
            # simplified: move ready permits to available
            self.cooldowns = [c for c in self.cooldowns if c[0] > now]
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
```

rob: Couple adjustments: add a max_backoff cap (30s) and ensure parse_retry_after respects server-sent header if >=1s. Also make cooldown adaptive: start at 800ms and exponentially increase if immediate subsequent 429s seen on same session.

ana: I'll update sample-app README and default config then. Suggestion: add a small CI stress test in devex pipeline that runs the onboarding flow and asserts the 99th-percentile rps stays under 4x baseline.

tina: My local numbers with these changes: peak rps dropped from ~950 to ~120 and the number of refreshes/second dropped from 8->1. I pushed a branch with unit tests for singleflight and parse_retry_after.

infra-bot: branch created tina/fix-py-refresh-singleflight, CI queued. :white_check_mark:

kai: I'll review the PR. If it's clean let's cut a patch release to py-sdk and update the sample-app template. Also add a small telemetry rumble to detect multi-refresh per minute per session so we can alert if this regresses.

tina: Thanks — will add telemetry. If reviewers approve I'll merge today.
